title: Deploy-eval decider and autorevert playbook with hysteresis
creator: Priya Raman
description: Goal: implement an autonomous decision layer ('deploy-eval decider') that runs during Canary and A/B rollouts and enacts an automatic rollback or hold when quality regressions are detected. This ticket covers the decision logic (statistical tests + hysteresis), the safety playbook for autorevert, integration points with the rollout controller, and the observability/DBG tooling needed to diagnose false positives. The system must be conservative (prefer brief holds and targeted reverts over noisy churn), explainable to SRE/PM, and testable end-to-end in staging and shadow traffic runs.
background_and_rationale: We frequently observe small but impactful regressions after config/model flips that escape manual review until customers complain. Existing canary guards trigger alerts but require human intervention, lengthening incident MTTR. An autonomous decider can reduce customer exposure and operational overhead by reverting when pre-defined quality gates breach for multiple evaluators, while using hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping on transient noise.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deploy-eval decider runs during Canary and A/B rollouts and evaluates metrics from eval pipelines within 60s of metric emission. 2) If a regression condition is met, the controller will automatically either hold the rollout or revert the new variant according to the playbook. 3) Hysteresis: must require two consecutive evaluation windows (configurable, default=3 minutes) before an auto-revert. 4) Explanations (metric diffs, p-values, sample counts) for every auto decision are recorded and visible in Console rollout trace. 5) End-to-end tests in staging that inject synthetic regressions must cause auto-reverts in >=95% of trials and produce a forensics artifact. 6) SLOs: decision latency <120s, false positive rate <1% on historical baseline.
design_overview: Decision inputs: streaming eval metrics (accuracy/agree/bleu/embedding-sim), latency percentiles, token-distribution anomalies, and feature-sliced KPIs. Primary statistical test: two-sided TOST for equivalence where applicable, fallback to bootstrap/confidence intervals for non-parametric metrics. Aggregation windows: 30s micro-window + configurable rolling window. Hysteresis controller: require N consecutive failed windows OR exceed a cumulative severity score threshold. Playbook actions: 1) hold (freeze traffic increase), 2) revert model/config, 3) route degraded cohort to legacy variant, 4) emergency alert (pager) if customer_impact=high. All actions include a cooldown and manual-approve override. We will expose thresholds per environment and per customer (dedicated vs hosted).
tradeoffs_and_considerations: - Aggressive auto-reverts reduce customer exposure but risk unnecessary rollbacks on noisy metrics; hysteresis and multi-metric voting mitigate this. - Running heavy stats in-line increases decision latency; we will prioritize lightweight approximations in hot path and run heavier diagnostics asynchronously for post-mortem. - Per-customer thresholds increase configuration surface; default profiles will cover 90% of customers with opt-in overrides.
integration_points: - Rollout controller API: pause/scale down/rollback endpoints. - Eval pipeline: streaming metrics topic (Kafka) + batch fallback. - Console: expose trace UI and allow manual override/reapply. - Audit logs: KMS-signed action records for Private deployments.
observability_and_metrics: Primary metrics consumed: eval.delta_score (signed), eval.p_value, eval.sample_count, latency.p95_delta, token_confidence_shift. Decision telemetry: decision_time_ms, action_taken (none/hold/revert/route), windows_failed_count, severity_score. Dashboards: per-rollout trace, cohort-sliced heatmap, and a global decisions feed for SRE. Alerting: anomaly on decision false-positive rate and decision latency.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for statistical primitives and hysteresis logic. 2) Integration test harness in staging that replays historical canary traces and injects controlled regressions. 3) Chaos experiment: simulate metric noise and verify hysteresis avoids flip-flop for at least the configured cooldown. 4) Blue/green shadow: run decision engine in 'observe-only' for 2 weeks on production traffic, compare to human decisions before flipping to active enforcement.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (observe-only): enable on 10% of non-customer-critical canaries for 2 weeks. Stage 2 (soft-enforce): allow 'hold' actions automatically, require manual approval for reverts for 1 week. Stage 3 (full-auto): enable automatic reverts with conservative defaults for all canaries; only escalate to pager when customer_impact=high. Each stage gated by: no more than 2 unexpected auto-holds per week, FP rate <1%, decision latency within SLO.
playbook_snippet: When the decider marks 'severe' then: 1) Freeze rollout scale to current traffic (hold). 2) Notify owner (channel + email) and create forensic artifact (metrics + sample prompts + model outputs). 3) After 3 consecutive failed windows, automatically revert to previous model variant and mark rollback in audit logs. 4) If rollback fails or customer_impact escalates, trigger on-call pager and start incident bridge. Manual unfreeze requires engineering approval and a follow-up rollout plan.

decisions: Use hysteresis (N consecutive failed windows) as primary anti-flap mechanism instead of exponential backoff.
Default enforce level: hold after first alarm, auto-revert after three consecutive fails.
Primary statistical test: TOST for numeric metrics; bootstrap for distributional metrics; use non-parametric if sample counts <50.
Expose per-customer thresholds but ship conservative defaults for hosted tier.
Run heavy diagnostics asynchronously and attach to the forensic artifact; keep fast decision path minimal.
notes: Follow-up items: add RBAC for who can change auto-revert thresholds, add canary-specific sample inflation heuristics, and build a lightweight simulator UI in Console for runbook rehearsals. Consider adding a ML model to predict likely false positives based on historical decision features in a later iteration.
